overall: The AG declined to review the untimely notice complaint about the Seekonk Street topic, found no violation for the April 10 minutes, and found no posting or filing requirement; it recommended but did not order amending the minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board discussed the Seekonk Street land sale at its April 10 meeting without listing it on the posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: Because the complaint was filed with the Board on November 29, we find that this allegation is untimely and we decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the April 10 minutes were inaccurate because they omitted the Seekonk Street discussion.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, because these minutes remained in draft form at the time this complaint was filed, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by creating inaccurate or insufficiently detailed minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant asserted the April 10 minutes were not properly posted or filed.
allegations.key_passage: we note that the Open Meeting Law does not require that public bodies post their meeting minutes to a website, or that minutes be filed with the Town Clerk.

allegations.summary: Not raised by the complainant: the AG noted the April 10 minutes were not approved until January 23, 2018, despite many intervening meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Board met regularly but did not approve its April 10 minutes until January 23, 2018, despite having met eighteen times between April and January.
